manuscript_claim: The public J-SHIS/NIED flatfile provides a large paired residual benchmark for Japanese K-NET and KiK-net records
primary_evidence_location: Main text: Results, Record scale and workflow; Fig. 1
numerical_anchor: 333,808 records; 2,581 station identifiers; 1,840 source identifiers; 322,061 basic-residual rows per target; 321,732 site-residual rows per target
interpretation_boundary: Scope: public flatfile subset sub1-v2024 and MF2013-supported records only; raw records are cited from NIED and are not redistributed in this package

manuscript_claim: MF2013 D1400/AVS30 site terms reduce residual error most strongly at 1--3 s
primary_evidence_location: Main text: Results, Long-period site-term gains; Fig. 2
numerical_anchor: MAE reductions: 1.6% PGA; 3.9% SA(0.3 s); 16.1% SA(1.0 s); 21.2% SA(3.0 s)
interpretation_boundary: Scope: paired residual comparison against MF2013 basic prediction; statement concerns residual reduction, not a new ground-motion equation

manuscript_claim: The official site terms absorb much of the long-period basin-depth station-residual structure
primary_evidence_location: Main text: Results, Station residuals identify site-structure proxies; Fig. 3
numerical_anchor: SA(3.0 s) station-residual Spearman rho with log10(D1400) changes from 0.614 to -0.025
interpretation_boundary: Scope: D1400 is a basin-depth proxy; three-dimensional basin-edge geometry and nonlinear response are outside the current evidence

manuscript_claim: The long-period site-term ordering is stable across network and source-type subsets
primary_evidence_location: Main text: Results, The period ordering is stable; Fig. 4
numerical_anchor: Positive SA(1.0 s) and SA(3.0 s) MAE reductions occur in K-NET, KiK-net, crustal, interplate, and intraplate subsets
interpretation_boundary: Scope: subgroup and bin checks support period ordering; they do not isolate all source-path-site interactions

manuscript_claim: Remaining station residuals after MF2013 site correction are predictable under held-out validation
primary_evidence_location: Main text: Results, Remaining station residuals are predictable; Fig. 6; Supplementary Fig. S2
numerical_anchor: Spatial-block RMSE reductions: 38.9% SA(1.0 s); 44.3% SA(3.0 s); seven-region SA(3.0 s) reduction 47.8% for full site-location model
interpretation_boundary: Scope: station-level residual correction experiment; it is not presented as a replacement ground-motion prediction model

manuscript_claim: SA(3.0 s) station multipliers change official long-period response-spectrum ordinates at matched station meshes
primary_evidence_location: Main text: Results, Station multipliers affect official long-period spectra; Fig. 8; Supplementary Fig. S3
numerical_anchor: 50-year 10% median SA(3.0 s) changes from 0.076 g to 0.048 g after applying station multipliers
interpretation_boundary: Scope: deterministic station-ordinate sensitivity on matched station meshes; source recurrence, logic-tree weights, and path terms remain fixed

manuscript_claim: An independent OpenQuake/GEM Japan-model calculation gives an engine-level check on the same multiplier concept
numerical_anchor: Representative-station baseline curves and deterministic SA(3.0 s) multiplier shifts are reported in OpenQuake-derived tables
interpretation_boundary: Scope: independent sensitivity calculation for representative stations; official J-SHIS production implementation remains outside this package

manuscript_claim: The public-parameter J-SHIS PBV audit makes the official-data interface traceable
primary_evidence_location: Main text: Methods and Results, public-parameter audit; Fig. 1E-F; Supplementary Figs. S5-S6
numerical_anchor: 10,467 sampled meshes; 41,868 official-threshold rows; zero failed rows; zero zero-probability rows; global RMSE 0.380 at official PBV thresholds
interpretation_boundary: Scope: public-parameter audit and diagnostic recomputation; final official J-SHIS hazard-map production calculation is not claimed

manuscript_claim: The sampled-grid SA(3.0 s) correction surface supports station-to-grid continuity over the audit mesh set
primary_evidence_location: Main text: Methods and Results, sampled-grid correction surface; Supplementary Fig. S10
numerical_anchor: Held-out station RMSE is 0.0678 log10 units; 70.7% reduction relative to zero correction; 10,467-mesh multiplier median 0.658
interpretation_boundary: Scope: sampled-grid interpolation using nearest-station public site proxies; source-level official hazard-map reproduction remains outside this package

manuscript_claim: Independent public-site audits support the basin and site-response interpretation at proxy level
primary_evidence_location: Main text: Methods, Results, and Discussion; Supplementary Figs. S7-S9, S11-S12, S15; Supplementary Table S27
numerical_anchor: Borehole profile coverage 98.6%; GSI terrain coverage 95.1%; VS400 join coverage 10,467/10,467; lowest-quartile gridded AVS30 tail-risk ratio 1.44; SA(3.0 s) site-variable model RMSE reduction 34.7% relative to zero correction
interpretation_boundary: Scope: proxy-level consistency from independent public products; the interpretable site-variable model recovers part of the long-period station term without resolving full three-dimensional basin response

manuscript_claim: Residual-tail structure is geographically and probability-level dependent in the public-parameter audit
primary_evidence_location: Main text: Results and Discussion; Supplementary Figs. S6-S8
numerical_anchor: Rows with |log10 residual| >= 0.70 account for 6.0% of all rows; 16.7% of sampled meshes have at least one tail row; strongest coarse geographic tail is northeast Hokkaido
interpretation_boundary: Scope: diagnostic residual-tail interpretation for sampled public-parameter rows; individual-mesh mechanism attribution requires additional source, path, and basin models

manuscript_claim: The release package separates original public inputs from derived outputs and documents what can be deposited
primary_evidence_location: Data availability; Code availability; Supplementary Table S6; public-archive readiness files
numerical_anchor: The release-candidate audit and smoke-test reports record the current file count, checksum, gate count, raw/cache scan, local-path scan, and private-planning text scan
interpretation_boundary: Scope: technical pre-deposition review; final author/legal approval, public repository URL, Zenodo DOI, funding, COI, and contribution statements remain required before submission

manuscript_claim: Multi-event paired KiK-net borehole/surface waveforms support the low-frequency part of the period target at proxy level
primary_evidence_location: Main text: Methods, Results, and Discussion; Fig. 8A; Supplementary Fig. S13; Supplementary Tables S21-S22
numerical_anchor: 460 event-station pairs from two events; median horizontal PGA ratio 1.458; 333 of 460 ratios exceed 1; median 0.2-0.5 Hz ratio 2.382 for the converted 2025 event and 1.053 for the 2026 ASCII event
interpretation_boundary: Scope: two-event transfer-function audit; nonlinear response, event-specific source/path separation, and complete KiK-net archive analysis remain outside this evidence

manuscript_claim: Northeast Hokkaido is the clearest regional residual-tail case in the public-parameter audit
primary_evidence_location: Main text: Results and Discussion; Fig. 8B; Supplementary Figs. S7-S9, S11-S12
numerical_anchor: Northeast-Hokkaido tail fraction 45.5% versus 7.3% outside the band; nearest-station median D1400 212 m versus 75 m outside the band
interpretation_boundary: Scope: regional source-site-basin diagnostic case; individual-mesh mechanism attribution requires additional source, path, basin-boundary, and waveform modeling

manuscript_claim: Station-correction terms propagate through the available official J-SHIS response-spectrum ordinates on the sampled audit grid
primary_evidence_location: Main text: Methods and Results; Supplementary Fig. S14; Supplementary Table S23
numerical_anchor: 10,467 sampled meshes; 334,944 mesh response rows; 50-year 10% median sampled-grid multipliers are 1.045, 0.966, 0.834, 0.720, and 0.658 at 0.3, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, and 3.0/5.0 s
interpretation_boundary: Scope: official-map response-spectrum propagation audit; source recurrence, path model, period-dependent sigma, spatial correlation, and logic-tree implementation remain official/fixed and are not reproduced source by source

manuscript_claim: The source-model boundary is documented with official J-SHIS 2024 PSHM input packages and sampled-grid public-parameter checks
primary_evidence_location: Main text: Methods and Results; Supplementary Tables S24 and S26
numerical_anchor: 421 CSV parameter files and 200 shapefile layers were inventoried; sampled-grid checks recompute 41,868 rows on 10,467 meshes
interpretation_boundary: Scope: public-parameter consistency check; validated national source-level production PSHA remains the official J-SHIS implementation

manuscript_claim: Representative city-nearest spectra and uncertainty intervals show the engineering scale of the official-spectrum shift
primary_evidence_location: Main text: Results; Fig. 8; Supplementary Table S25
numerical_anchor: 50-year 10% SA(3.0 s) changes by -34.6% in Tokyo, -42.4% in Osaka, -1.0% in Sapporo, -37.2% in Sendai, and -16.8% in the northeast-Hokkaido/Soya case; bootstrap median shift CI is -38.5% to -37.4%
interpretation_boundary: Scope: representative nearest-station sensitivity examples and bootstrap/fold uncertainty summaries; they do not replace site-specific engineering analysis
